goal: Decide whether one text message is likely a scam, likely safe, or uncertain, and explain why in plain words an older adult can understand.

message.text: ＩＲＳ: your tax refund is on hold. Pay the release fee with g1ft c@rds or g i f t - c a r d s from any store.

explanation: This looks like a scam. The message asks you to pay with a gift card, which is a strong warning sign. Government agencies like the IRS never ask for gift cards. Do not reply or send money.
what_to_do: Do not reply, do not tap any link, and do not send money or codes. If you are worried, call IRS at 1-800-555-0103 (from our trusted list).
guide_tip: Tip from our guide (G01): Do not buy the card. Hang up or delete the text and call the agency using the number on your card or letter.
